name: Write a Short Drama Episode with Character Profiles
prompt:
Write a short drama script episode and character profiles. Save results to the specified files.

Drama premise: A young woman discovers her boss is her long-lost sibling.
Genre: Modern romance/drama
Format: Vertical short-form drama (each episode 1-3 minutes)
Episode number: Episode 1 (the hook)

Task 1: Save character profiles to `characters.json` as an array of exactly 3 characters. Each character object must have:
- `name` (string): character full name
- `role` (string): one of "protagonist", "antagonist", "supporting"
- `age` (integer): character age
- `personality_traits` (array of exactly 3 strings): personality keywords
- `motivation` (string): what drives this character
- `conflict` (string): the character's main conflict in this drama

Task 2: Save the episode script to `episode_01.md`. The script must have:
- A title line at the top: `# Episode 1: [episode title]`
- A scene setting block starting with `SCENE:` describing location and time
- At least 6 lines of dialogue in the format `CHARACTER_NAME: dialogue text`
- A cliffhanger ending marked with `[CLIFFHANGER]` on its own line
- Total length between 150 and 400 words

Task 3: Save a hook analysis to `hook_analysis.json`:
{
  "hook_type": "<one of: mystery, conflict, revelation, cliffhanger>",
  "hook_description": "<string describing what makes the opening 3 seconds compelling>",
  "emotional_triggers": ["<at least 2 emotion words>"],
  "target_audience": "<string>",
  "episode_end_type": "cliffhanger"
}

Save all files in the current working directory.

criteria.description: characters.json exists as a readable file in the working directory.
characters.json is a JSON array containing exactly 3 character objects.
Every character object has all six required fields: name, role, age (integer), personality_traits (array), motivation, and conflict.
All character roles are valid (protagonist, antagonist, or supporting) and at least one character has the role 'protagonist'.
criteria.testPattern: roles include protagonist.*supporting|character roles are valid

criteria.description: Every character's personality_traits array has exactly 3 non-empty string entries.
episode_01.md exists as a readable file in the working directory.
episode_01.md has an H1 heading whose text (lowercased) contains 'episode 1'.
episode_01.md contains at least 6 lines in 'UPPERCASE_NAME: dialogue text' format.
criteria.testPattern: contains at least 6 lines of dialogue in 'NAME: text' format

criteria.description: episode_01.md contains the literal marker '[CLIFFHANGER]' on its own line.
hook_analysis.json exists with a valid hook_type (mystery/conflict/revelation/cliffhanger), at least 2 emotional_triggers strings, and episode_end_type set to 'cliffhanger'.
criteria.testPattern: hook_analysis.json > file exists|hook type and emotional triggers

eval.rubric:
Context: The agent was asked to write a short drama episode about a woman discovering her boss is her long-lost sibling.

Criterion 1: Script Dramatic Quality (Weight: 60%)
1.0: The episode has a compelling opening that immediately establishes tension, the dialogue reveals character personality and advances the plot, and the cliffhanger ending creates genuine suspense. Character voices are distinct and the premise (boss = sibling) is set up naturally.
0.5: Script follows the format but dialogue is generic or the cliffhanger is weak.
0: Script does not address the premise or has no dramatic tension.

Criterion 2: Character Development (Weight: 40%)
1.0: Character profiles are specific and internally consistent. Motivations are meaningful and link to the drama's central conflict. Personality traits are distinct across the 3 characters (no two characters have the same traits).
0.5: Characters are defined but motivations are vague or traits are generic.
0: Characters are missing or do not connect to the drama's plot.
eval.name: Quality Judge
